Welcome to ArchiveNews, for all the news that's worth saving.

How it works

Use archive.is to archive a webpage URL, specifically a news article. For example, say I want to submit this article on why Pluto will remain a dwarf planet. Instead of submitting the URL directly linking to The Huffington Post, head to archive.is and archive the news article by pasting the URL into the archive bar. Archive.is will load the webpage you pasted into an archived form (this step can take a while), and will provide you with a link for sharing. Take the archive link and use that as your submission link.

Step-by-step

  1. Find a news article you wish to share (example).
  2. Head over to archive.is and paste the URL to the orginal news article in the box, then press "submit URL".
  3. Wait for archive.is to load the article into an archived format. This may take a while.
  4. Once it has created the archived article, it should look like this.
  5. Take the URL to the archived article and submit it as a link here on /v/ArchiveNews, and you're done!

Why it matters

Simply put, an author can edit an article at any given point after submitting it, and linking to the original article's URL may take new readers to that editted article. When you archive an article it creates a copy of the original article that stays the same 100% of the time and any edits the author makes to the original article will not affect the archived article. Archiving is a failsafe method of sharing a news article without that article being modified or removed.
